requirement: Identify the governing public pair as the official NCT05832918 uploads titled Effects of core stability exercises and cognitive tasks compared to general exercises and cognitive tasks on chronic non-specific back pain, consisting of a five-page protocol and separate one-page statistical-analysis document both dated 27 March 2023; keep the reference analysis document annotation-only and confirm the registry binding because neither PDF prints the NCT identifier.

evidence.text: The protocol prints the exact study title and date 03, 27, 2023 but no NCT identifier.
The separate statistical-analysis page repeats the exact title and date but no NCT identifier.

notes: The official ClinicalTrials.gov file paths provide the NCT binding; a second reviewer must confirm that provenance before release.

requirement: Describe a prospective randomized parallel-group exercise study comparing core-stability exercise plus cognitive tasks with general exercise plus the same cognitive-task program in people with chronic nonspecific low-back pain.

evidence.text: The objectives compare the two exercise programs, and the methods state that patients will be randomly divided into intervention and control groups.

requirement: Define the analysis population as consented patients with chronic nonspecific low-back pain who pass eligibility and cognitive screening, and confirm the complete age, diagnostic, pain, MMSE, neurologic, vision, hearing, vestibular, surgical and lower-extremity eligibility boundary before finalization rather than inventing details absent from the protocol PDF.
acceptable_values: complete boundary confirmed from governing source

evidence.text: The protocol describes clinic sampling, eligibility review, informed consent and completion of demographic information and MMSE but does not list the full eligibility criteria.

requirement: Before finalization, specify the allocation ratio, sequence-generation method, any blocking or stratification, allocation concealment, enrollment and assignment roles, and outcome-assessor masking; do not infer these operational details from the word randomized alone.

evidence.text: The protocol says patients will be randomly divided into two groups but supplies no operational randomization or masking procedure.

requirement: Represent the intervention as six weeks with three sessions per week while preserving the stated total of 16 sessions, and resolve this arithmetic conflict before defining exposure, adherence or the immediate post-treatment visit.

evidence.text: The methods state treatment for six weeks at three sessions a week and then state For sixteen sessions.

requirement: Distinguish the two programs operationally: CSE targets local transverse-abdominal and lumbar-multifidus activation at about 30% maximal contraction with pressure biofeedback, whereas GE recruits abdominal flexors and lumbar extensors at about 60%-70%, with planned exercise times of 20 and 14 minutes respectively.

evidence.text: The protocol contrasts local-muscle CSE with global-muscle GE, gives contraction targets and specifies 20 versus 14 minutes.

requirement: Apply exercise without cognitive tasks in sessions 1-4 and add the same progressively changing cognitive-task program to both groups in sessions 5-16, retaining the protocol's session-specific reverse-order, counting, Stroop, recall and N-back tasks.
acceptable_values: same cognitive program in both groups

evidence.text: The protocol assigns no cognitive tasks for the first four sessions and a common detailed cognitive program from sessions 5 through 16.

requirement: Reconcile the primary-endpoint hierarchy before finalization: the protocol calls both pain intensity measured by VAS and disability measured by ODI primary at baseline, post-intervention and three-month follow-up, so state whether they are co-primary or whether one is primary and the other supportive.

evidence.text: The primary objectives and primary outcome section name pain and disability and schedule both before, after and three months after intervention.

requirement: Operationalize VAS and ODI with instrument version, scoring range, direction, valid-item rule, baseline and follow-up derivations and clinically interpretable effect scale; do not invent these details because the protocol names the instruments without complete scoring rules.

evidence.text: The protocol names VAS and ODI as primary measures but does not provide their full scoring or missing-item algorithms.

requirement: Retain the prespecified secondary families: postural stability, stabilogram-diffusion control, fear of movement, fear-avoidance beliefs and quality of life, while labeling their analyses secondary or exploratory rather than silently promoting them to primary status.

evidence.text: The secondary objectives and outcome section list the postural-control and patient-reported outcome families.

requirement: For force-platform outcomes, use 100-Hz center-of-pressure recordings in the eight firm/foam by eyes-open/closed by cognitive-task/no-task conditions, five 60-second trials per condition, and average the five trials after applying the stated trial-validity and repeat rule.

evidence.text: The protocol specifies the eight crossed standing conditions, 100-Hz acquisition, five 60-second trials, trial averaging and repetition when the cognitive-count error is at least three.

requirement: Derive stabilogram-diffusion outcomes over lags from 0 through 10 seconds as short-term and long-term mean-squared-displacement slopes plus the critical time and critical displacement where the open-loop and closed-loop regions meet.

evidence.text: The data-analysis section defines the stabilogram diffusion graph, its open- and closed-loop slopes and critical-point coordinates.

requirement: Low-pass filter center-of-pressure signals at 10 Hz and derive anterior-posterior range as absolute Y maximum minus Y minimum, mediolateral range as absolute X maximum minus X minimum, mean total-sway velocity and total sway area, with units and artifact handling confirmed.

evidence.text: The protocol gives the 10-Hz filter and the four linear COP measures, including the two range formulas, but not units or artifact rules.

requirement: Define randomized efficacy, intervention-exposed safety and postural-evaluable analysis sets and treatment attribution, including never-treated participants, session nonadherence, treatment switching, incomplete follow-up, invalid force-platform trials and withdrawal.

evidence.text: The protocol describes randomization, repeated sessions, follow-up and trial repetition but neither source defines analysis populations.

requirement: Define the CSE-plus-cognitive versus GE-plus-cognitive estimand for each selected primary endpoint, including target population, repeated outcome variable, group-by-time contrast, population summary and strategies for exercise discontinuation, nonadherence, concomitant therapy, missing outcome and death.
acceptable_values: CSE plus cognitive versus GE plus cognitive

evidence.text: The protocol poses randomized longitudinal comparisons but does not define estimand attributes or intercurrent-event strategies.

requirement: Use a participant-level repeated-measures model that directly estimates the randomized group-by-time contrast for each selected primary endpoint, extending the reference mixed-model ANOVA to the protocol's baseline, immediate post-treatment and three-month visits and specifying participant effect, covariance, degrees of freedom and contrasts.

evidence.text: The reference proposes mixed-model ANOVA for two groups, two situations and two times but does not identify all protocol timepoints or an executable covariance model.
Pain and disability are scheduled before, after and three months after intervention.

requirement: Apply distributional diagnostics to model residuals and transformations only when prespecified and interpretable; if Stata's ladder-of-powers procedure is retained, document the selection rule, transformed-scale model and valid back-transformation of effects and confidence intervals rather than testing every raw variable with Shapiro-Wilk as an automatic gate.

evidence.text: The reference applies Shapiro-Wilk to all variables, then Stata Gladder transformation and return to the raw scale without an operational selection or back-transformation rule.

requirement: Replace or supplement the reference's Friedman fallback with a robust analysis that preserves the between-group randomized contrast and repeated participant observations, and specify how ties, missing visits and multiple postural conditions are handled.

evidence.text: The reference names Friedman for nonnormal variables but does not explain how it estimates the randomized two-group treatment contrast.

requirement: Specify outcome-specific missing-data handling for absent baseline, post-treatment or three-month questionnaires, incomplete sessions, invalid or repeated force-platform trials and partially missing conditions; state the primary assumption and at least one sensitivity analysis for informative dropout.

evidence.text: The design creates repeated questionnaire, session, trial and condition data, but neither document defines missing-data handling.

requirement: Define the confirmatory endpoint family and multiplicity control across pain, disability, visits, postural variables, eight standing conditions and patient-reported secondary outcomes; do not treat within-group Bonferroni post-hoc tests as sufficient control of the randomized study-wide family.

evidence.text: The protocol defines two primary objectives and many longitudinal secondary measures and conditions without an inferential hierarchy.
The reference specifies Bonferroni only for within-group post-hoc changes.

requirement: Clarify whether the reference's P<0.05 convention is two-sided, align alpha and confidence levels with the declared endpoint family and report adjusted or exploratory interpretation as applicable.

evidence.text: The reference declares P less than 0.05 significant without sidedness, confidence intervals or study-wide family alignment.

requirement: Use the prospective target of 34 total participants derived from 26 analyzable participants, 13 per group, after a 30% dropout allowance, based on ODI with effect size 0.3, correlation 0.5, three measurements, 90% power and 5% type-I error; do not substitute later registry enrollment targets as the prospective calculation.

evidence.text: The protocol gives the G*Power ODI calculation, assumptions, 26-participant analyzable target and 34-person dropout-inflated target.

notes: Any later registry target is conduct context and must not replace this document's prospective target.

requirement: Define exercise safety and tolerability summaries using exposed-participant denominators and participant and event counts, including pain exacerbation, falls, inability to complete a session or force-platform condition, intervention modification and discontinuation by randomized group.

evidence.text: The protocol involves repeated exercise and demanding standing/cognitive conditions but neither source specifies a safety analysis.

requirement: Before finalization, confirm the prerecruitment governance and official-registry binding, reconcile the 16-session versus six-week/three-session schedule and endpoint hierarchy, and provide effect estimates with confidence intervals, small-sample inference, diagnostics, fallbacks and reproducible coding in the stated SPSS 21 and Stata 13.0 software; present unresolved choices as questions rather than facts.

evidence.text: The dated protocol supplies design, schedule, outcomes and sample size but has internal schedule and hierarchy ambiguities and no NCT printed.
The reference names SPSS 21, Stata 13.0, distribution tests, mixed ANOVA, Bonferroni, Friedman and P less than 0.05 but omits effect intervals and executable model details.
